'''María Antonia Herrero''' (born 1978) is a chemist who works in the faculty of [[Chemistry|chemical sciences]] at the [[University of Castilla–La Mancha]] (UCLM) in [[Ciudad Real]]. Her work focuses on chemical [[nanomaterials]], with research undertaken at the same university.<ref name="wo">{{cite web|url=http://www.woman.es/galerias/lifestyle/la-ciencia-en-femenino?id=3|title=Mª Antonia Herrero|website=woman.es|access-date=2016-07-05|archive-date=2018-04-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180410202133/https://www.woman.es/galerias/lifestyle/la-ciencia-en-femenino?id=3|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="cm">{{cite web|url=https://cmccurso1011.wikispaces.com/Cient%C3%ADficas+espa%C3%B1olas|title=cmccurso1011 - Científicas españolas|website=cmccurso1011.wikispaces.com}}</ref>

==Life==
Herrero began her doctorate in 2000, on microwaves and Sustainable Chemistry Group of the University of Castilla–La Mancha, working in aided by organic reactions [[Microwave|microwaves.]] Part of her thesis was done in Uppsala, Sweden after which she earned her doctorate in 2006.<ref name="ms">{{cite web|url=http://www.msocnanochemistrygroup.com/mar%C3%ADa-antonia.html|title=Nanochemistry Group UCLM|website=Nanochemistry Group UCLM|access-date=2016-07-05|archive-date=2018-06-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180614172527/http://www.msocnanochemistrygroup.com/mar%C3%ADa-antonia.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Research==
Her work centres on the study of the applications of [[nanomaterials]], specifically [[nanotube]]s, that can be modified for distinct uses in such diverse fields as medicine (e.g. as conveyors of drugs to treat illnesses like [[cancer]] or [[Alzheimer's disease]]).<ref name="wo"/><ref name="cm"/> After she joined the nano-chemistry group at UCLM, her research focused on [[microwave radiation]] for the activation of carbon [[nanostructures]] in [[solvent]]-free conditions, developing multifunctional synthetic materials to be used in science and biological applications. She has authored over 35 scientific publications, some book chapters and holds four scientific patents.<ref name="ti">{{cite web|url=https://umsoc.com/staff/dr-maria-antonia-herrero-chamorro/|title=Dra. María Antonia Herrero Chamorro|date=11 January 2011|website=umsoc.com}}</ref>

In 2012, María Antonia Herrero obtained a grant from the Iberdrola Foundation to develop a project in the field of energy and the environment. The project, headed by Herrero, proposed the preparation of a device that uses solar energy to produce electricity and wastewater regeneration through integrated electrochemical processes fed by renewable energies, thus contributing to the fight against climate change.<ref name="new">{{cite web|url=http://www.uclm.es/gabinete/ver_noticias.asp?id_noticia=7658|title=Información no disponible|first=Universidad de Castilla-La|last=Mancha|website=www.uclm.es|access-date=2016-07-05|archive-date=2016-03-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307164918/http://www.uclm.es/gabinete/ver_noticias.asp?id_noticia=7658|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In July 2016 she published research on ''Design of Assembled Systems Based on Conjugated Polyphenylene Derivatives and Carbon Nanohorns.''<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/305272841|title=Design of Assembled Systems Based on Conjugated Polyphenylene Derivatives and Carbon Nanohorns|first1=Daniel|last1=Iglesias|first2=Javier|last2=Guerra|first3=M|last3=Victoria Gómez|first4=Antonio|last4=Rodriguez Garcia|first5=Pilar|last5=Prieto|first6=Ester|last6=Vázquez|first7=Maria|last7=Herrero|date=1 July 2016|journal=Chemistry - A European Journal|volume=22|issue=33 |pages=11643–11651 |via=ResearchGate|doi=10.1002/chem.201601282|pmid=27404562 |hdl=10578/11774|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

==Recent publications==
* Functional motor recovery from brain ischemic insult by carbon nanotube-mediated siRNA silencing, PNAS, 108, 10952–10957, 2011.
* Chirality dependent charge transfer events in individual semiconducting single wall carbon nanotubes – (9,4), (8,6), (8,7), and (9,7), J. Am. Chem. Soc., 133, 18696–18706, 2011.
* Few-Layer graphenes from ball-milling of graphite with melamine, ChemComm, 47, 10936–10938, 2011.
* Carbon nanohorns functionalized with polyamidoamine dendrimers as efficient biocarrier materials for gene therapy. Carbon, 50, 2832–2844, (2012).
* Enhanced docetaxel-mediated cytotoxicity in human prostate cancer cells through knockdown of cofilin-1 by carbon nanohorn delivered siRNA. Biomaterials, 33, 8152–8159, (2012).
* Degree of Chemical Functionalization of Carbon Nanotubes Determines Tissue Distribution and Excretion Profile.Angewandte Chemie, 124, 6495–6499, (2012).
* In vivo degradation of functionalized carbon nanotubes after stereotactic administration in the brain cortex. Nanomedicine, 10, 1485–1494, (2012).
* Asbestos-like pathogenicity of long carbon nanotubes can be alleviated by chemical functionalization. Angewandte Chemie. DOI: 10.1002/anie.201207664

===Book chapters=== 
*Recent Advances in Covalent Functionalization and Characterization of Carbon Nanotubes, Chapter 9: Fundamentals and ApplicHandbook of Carbon Nano Materials, {{ISBN|978-981-4350-20-4}}, 271–324, 2011.
*Reproducibility and scalability of Microwave-Assisted Reactions, Chapter in  Fundamentals and Microwave heating (2011), {{ISBN|978-953-308-337-7}}.

==Awards==
In November 2010, she was awarded, along with four other scientists ([[Isabel Lastres Becker]], [[Ana Briones Alonso]], [[Mercedes Vila]] and [[Elena Ramírez Parra]]), the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science]], with an endowment of €15000 each. This award rewards the work of women scientists under 40.<ref name="cu">{{cite web|url=http://www.culturabiotec.com/2011/02/prada/|title=La investigación "se viste de Prada" - Cultura Biotec|website=www.culturabiotec.com|access-date=2016-07-05|archive-date=2018-09-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180929233359/http://www.culturabiotec.com/2011/02/prada/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="pais">{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/sociedad/2010/11/18/actualidad/1290034810_850215.html|title=Cinco científicas de la vida españolas reciben las becas L'Oréal-Unesco|last=M.R.E|newspaper=El País |date=18 November 2010|via=elpais.com}}</ref><ref name="new"/>

In 2011, she received the "Ibn Wafid of Toledo" Prize, named after 10th-century Toledo physician [[Ibn Wafid|Abenguefit]], for young researchers from [[Castile-La Mancha]]. In 2012, the Iberdrola Foundation granted her an important line of investigation with the main subject of integration of carbon nanomaterials into solar cells.<ref name="ms"/>
